h: Holmes and Watson meet and take their first case, a deduction-driven London murder with a long flashback detour into the American West.

like.r: An earlier Victorian detective novel with a stolen jewel, many narrators and a slower, chattier pace than Doyle.
A Holmes-like friar reasons his way through murders in a medieval abbey, with far more learning and far less speed.
The same pair of friends turned into a bare-knuckle action romp, louder and looser with the canon.

h: Holmes is called to a fog-bound Devon moor where a family curse and a spectral dog seem to be killing the heirs one by one.

like.r: Another brooding English estate where the past presses on the living, with more psychological dread than detection.
A bleak, misty haunting told in a Victorian manner, creepier and shorter with no brilliant detective to save anyone.
Also a closed circle of suspects under growing menace, but cooler, tighter and built as a puzzle.

h: Twelve compact cases of blackmail, disguise and clever inference, each solved in one sitting by the detective everyone imitates.

like.r: A fair-play puzzle in the same tradition, built on one long case instead of a dozen short ones.
Short, paradoxical cases solved by a mild priest, whimsical where Holmes is brisk and scientific.
A classic Basil Rathbone-era screen Holmes if you want the stories acted rather than read.

h: Hercule Poirot arrives in a country house where a rich widow has been poisoned and every relative had a reason; the debut of the genre's queen.

like.r: Another Golden Age debut with a fussy, funny amateur sleuth, a touch more snobbish and chatty.
A modern country-house poisoning with a drawling detective and a family of suspects, sharper on class.
The detective who made Poirot possible, starting the same way: a brilliant outsider and his foil.

h: A snowbound train, a stabbed millionaire and twelve passengers who all lie; Poirot works the problem from the inside out.

like.r: A houseful of suspects, secrets and a rising body count, played as farce instead of cold-blooded puzzle.
The modern heir to the form: a house full of suspects and a detective who sees what everyone else misses.

like.t: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
like.r: A country-house puzzle taken to maze-like extremes, far stranger and more demanding than a train.

h: Ten strangers on an island, a nursery rhyme, and a killer working down the list; the template for every closed-circle thriller since.

like.r: A mansion full of suspects and a rising body count, played for farce rather than dread.
A modern snowbound lodge, shifting narrators and a killer among old friends, much in Christie's debt.
Gothic menace and a lonely English setting, with a detective at its center instead of none.

h: A village doctor narrates the murder of a wealthy neighbour while a retired Poirot grows turnips; the fair-play trick that still divides readers.

like.r: A village mystery of the same vintage and chatter, with Miss Marple instead of Poirot.

like.t: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
like.r: A fiendish country-house whodunit that plays tricks with who is telling the story.
A shooting-weekend murder among aristocrats and servants, with the class sharpness the Golden Age mostly avoided.

h: A honeymooning heiress is shot aboard a steamer on the Nile, and her ex-friend's jealousy is the least of the secrets on board.

like.r: A confined, glamorous cast and a cunning solution, in cold rather than heat.
A similarly crowded cast of beautiful suspects with money motives, set in the present.
A tale of a young wife outshone by someone else, darker and more psychological than Christie's puzzle.

h: A hated colonel is shot in the vicar's study, and the village's gossipy spinster turns out to be the sharpest mind for miles.

like.r: Retirees in an English village do the policing, a warm modern cousin with more jokes and more ache.
Another gentle small-community detective series built on common sense and tea.
A cheerful screen Miss Marple, if you want the character acted rather than read.

h: A killer sends Poirot taunting letters and works through the alphabet town by town; a serial-killer puzzle with a very Christie sting.

like.r: A modern take on the same duel with a murderer, much grislier and more psychological.
The same author's other great killer-with-a-plan puzzle, but sealed on an island.
A killer working through a pattern, with the cleverness turned bleak and wet.

h: A stranger's corpse turns up in a London bathtub wearing only a pince-nez; Lord Peter Wimsey, bored aristocrat, takes the case for fun.

like.r: The other great Golden Age debut, with a fussier sleuth and a more domestic puzzle.
Another witty amateur-sleuth pairing, American and boozy where Wimsey is arch and aristocratic.
The same English class order and chatty drawing rooms, with a corpse and a satirical eye.

h: Harriet Vane returns to her Oxford college where poison-pen letters are spooking the women; a campus mystery that is really a long courtship.

like.r: Another Oxbridge-flavoured campus world of intellect and menace, but American and far bleaker.
A literate British detective novel with a romantic aristocrat and a working partner, more modern and darker.
The slow-matured second chance at love that Gaudy Night turns into its emotional engine.

h: Philip Marlowe is hired by a dying millionaire to fix his wild daughters' mess, and the wisecracking narration is the real draw.

like.r: Los Angeles rot and a private eye out of his depth, with a plot even bleaker than Chandler's.
The harder, flatter ancestor of the Marlowe voice, with less poetry and more cold nerve.
Bogart and Bacall trade innuendo through a plot nobody can fully explain, and it does not matter.

h: A hulking ex-con hires Marlowe to find a girl who vanished years ago, and the search drags him through nightclubs and smoke-filled rooms.

like.r: A leaner, crueler tale of lust and murder on the California roadside, with no detective to hold it together.
The same city's rot, but modern and brutal, with three cops instead of one private eye.
Chandler co-wrote it: the same fatalistic voice and shadowy California, tighter and meaner.

h: Marlowe befriends a drunk war veteran, then gets dragged into a death among the rich; Chandler's most personal, wounded book.

like.r: A shambling, moody 1970s Marlowe that argues with the book, unusual and absorbing in its own right.
The earlier, harder private-eye foundation, with colder motives and less self-pity.
A later heir in the same tradition, set among Black Los Angeles in 1948 with a very human hero.

h: Sam Spade loses his partner and gets entangled with liars chasing a priceless statuette; hard-boiled prose with nothing wasted.

like.r: A famously faithful adaptation that more or less defined film noir on the screen.
A more lyrical, wisecracking private eye on the same sun-baked streets, with stranger plotting.
A 1970s homage to this world that adds civic corruption and a sense of doom.

h: A retired detective and his rich, wise-cracking wife drink their way through a missing-inventor case; hard-boiled plot, screwball marriage.

like.r: William Powell and Myrna Loy made the banter even more intoxicating on screen.
Another amateur sleuth with a sharp tongue and a bored manner, English and more mannered.
A crisp modern whodunit with a wicked sense of humour.

h: A charming nobody sent to Italy to fetch a rich man's son slides into forgery, murder and impersonation, and the reader roots for him.

like.r: A sun-soaked French adaptation that makes Ripley's envy as seductive as his crimes.
Another study of an outsider drawn to a gilded circle and willing to kill for belonging.
A quieter story of someone stepping into another's place, with a gothic rather than sly tone.

h: Two strangers meet on a train and one proposes swapping murders; Highsmith's debut makes a clean bargain into a long nightmare.

like.r: Hitchcock's version is slicker and gives the villain a showier menace.
The author's more famous amoral charmer, with a bigger canvas and a more seductive killer.
Another tale of two people tied by a murder that seemed easy, with fatalistic noir wit.

t: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
h: A burnt-out agent takes one last job in the Cold War and discovers how little the game cares about the people playing it.

like.r: The author's longer, more intricate mole hunt, with a wearied hero in the same grey world.
Another bruised post-war story of betrayal in a divided city, shot in expressionist shadows.
A Soviet investigator's murder case through the other side of the Cold War, grimmer and more procedural.

h: A retired spy is called back to unmask a Soviet mole inside British intelligence; patient, melancholic and rewarding for the attentive.

like.r: A hushed, handsome adaptation that trusts viewers to keep up with a sprawl of names and flashbacks.
Same period and tradecraft, but pure procedural suspense with far less melancholy.
A different era but a similar ritual of piecing together a hidden truth through endless talk.

h: Bond's first mission pits him against a financier at the baccarat table; leaner, nastier and more human than the films that followed.

like.r: A reboot that returns to the source's grit and gives Bond a bruising emotional arc.
A colder, procedural take on assassins and security services, with no gadgets or glamour.
A later spy-thriller with more explosions, fewer drinks and a hero who does not know who he is.

h: A Sicilian-American crime family fights for survival as a reluctant son is pulled into the business; pulpier and more sprawling than the film.

like.r: The film trims the subplots and gives the same story a solemn, operatic gravity.
Mob life from the foot-soldier's side, fast and funny where Puzo is stately.
Neighborhood loyalty, buried crime and the cost of both, quieter and more tragic than a mob epic.

h: A retired profiler is pulled back to hunt a killer who stalks families by the moon, with Hannibal Lecter caged in the margins.

like.r: A tighter, more famous sibling that brings Lecter forward and follows a young trainee.
A killer with a grand design, and detectives who realise too late what they are in.
A forensic chase with an immobile genius, more gadget-driven and less psychological.

h: An FBI trainee trades confidences with a brilliant imprisoned cannibal for a lead on a killer who skins women; chilling and swift.

like.r: A rare adaptation that matches the book's menace, with Hopkins and Foster at their peak.

like.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
like.r: A damaged investigator and a sexual predator case, Nordic and bigger in scope.
Darker still and more despairing, a killer who sees himself as a moralist.

h: Three very different LAPD cops tumble into a massacre case that leads through tabloids, hustlers and their own bosses; clipped and brutal.

like.r: A smart adaptation that boils the sprawling plot down while keeping the rot.
The author's earlier, more obsessive Hollywood-murder novel, no less bleak and a little more romantic.
A leaner, more elegant study of Los Angeles corruption with the same sense of doom.

h: Two boxer-cops fall for the same woman while chasing the real-life butchered starlet whose murder consumes them both.

like.r: A wider, crueller Los Angeles with more cops and a more satisfying shape.
A real-life case that eats the people hunting it, drier and more factual than Ellroy's fever dream.
The older, wittier Los Angeles detective novel that Ellroy twists into something savage.

h: Easy Rawlins, a laid-off Black veteran, takes a favour job to save his mortgage and ends up in a white woman's disappearance in 1948 Watts.

like.r: A rich period adaptation with Denzel Washington as Easy and a magnetic Don Cheadle.
The Los Angeles private-eye mold Mosley bends toward a Black protagonist and real stakes.
Not a mystery, but a Black American voice rendered with the same intimacy and force.

h: Three Boston boyhood friends, one abducted decades ago, are tied together again when a daughter is murdered; grief with a police case on top.

like.r: A somber, stacked-cast adaptation that keeps the book's moral weight.
An earlier Boston crime novel with the same ethical bruising around a missing child.
Loyalty and violence in tight communities, but grander and more stylised.

h: Two Boston private eyes hunt a missing four-year-old, and the case slowly forces them to choose between the law and what is right.

like.r: A faithful, grimy adaptation that keeps the book's central dilemma intact.
A bigger, more tragic Lehane novel that traces how one crime echoes for decades.
A missing-child case where the investigator's own past is the real puzzle.

h: A US marshal investigates a patient's disappearance from an island asylum during a hurricane, and nothing about the place adds up.

like.r: Scorsese leans into the paranoia and noir texture, with DiCaprio at his most haunted.
An older house-bound mystery where a haunted mind and an uncanny setting pull at the reader.
A therapy-centered mystery with a mute patient and a twist, slighter but just as hungry for surprise.

h: LAPD detective Harry Bosch investigates a body in a drainage pipe that links to his own Vietnam tunnel past; the template for the modern procedural.

like.r: The same city from the defence side, wittier and driven by courtroom manoeuvres.
A lone outsider breaking a conspiracy with muscle, more cartoonish and much less procedural.
A big, sombre Los Angeles crime epic with cops and thieves as mirror images.

h: A defence attorney who works from the back of his Lincoln takes on a rich client and finds himself being played by a smarter guilty man.

like.r: Matthew McConaughey sells the slick, rumpled lawyer in a brisk adaptation.
A lawyer slowly realising who he works for, with a more paranoid, big-money edge.
A more serious and morally tangled legal thriller, with a lawyer himself in the dock.

h: Jack Reacher steps off a bus in a sleepy Georgia town and is arrested for a murder, then starts pulling threads nobody wants pulled.

like.r: A bigger-scale, technical page-turner with a competent hero, heavier on hardware than fists.
A one-man army in a trap, played for wisecracks and sweat.
A grounded detective novel in place of one-man-army fantasy, with quieter moral rhythm.

t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
h: A disgraced journalist and a hacker with a vicious past dig into a decades-old disappearance inside a rich industrial family.

like.r: More Nordic cold and a killer, with a broken detective who drinks too much and shows up late.

like.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
like.r: A sleek English-language remake with an icy score and a stark Lisbeth.
A tighter, more claustrophobic hunt for a predator, with another damaged young heroine.

h: Oslo's most disastrous detective, Harry Hole, hunts a killer who leaves snowmen at the homes of vanished mothers.

like.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
like.r: Another icy Scandinavian bestseller, with a bigger conspiracy and hacker-journalist duo.
The classic hunt for a serial killer that this sort of novel owes a debt to.
A bleaker single-night version of the chase, rain-soaked and unforgiving.

h: A Dublin detective who lost his friends as a boy in the same woods investigates a girl's murder there; literary, haunting and deliberately unfinished.

like.r: Another beautifully written, slow, character-led crime story that cares more about guilt than the case.
A damaged investigator returns to a small town, shorter and sharper-edged than French.
Childhood trauma and a new killing in the same neighbourhood, with a grittier American voice.

h: A marriage narrated by two people who are both lying to you, with a midpoint turn that rewires everything before it.

like.r: The same poisoned-family dread from the same author, with a narrator who harms herself more than anyone else.
Another marriage haunted by an absent woman, told slower and wrapped in gothic fog instead of cable news.
The author's own screenplay keeps the book's structure and adds an icy, precise chill of its own.

h: A scarred reporter goes home to cover the murders of two girls and gets drawn back into her mother's house and her own wounds.

like.r: The bigger, more twisty breakout from the same writer, slicker and funnier.
A damaged investigator returned to a haunted place, richer in language and slower.
Another small community hiding violence behind pretty surfaces, with a lighter, more comic touch.

h: A woman whose brother was jailed for the family massacre she survived as a child is paid to reopen the case, and the evidence rots under her.

like.r: The same author's other bleak small-town book, shorter and less sprawling.
The real Kansas killings, filmed in stark black-and-white and far more austere.
A damaged woman and a memory she cannot trust, more commuter-friendly than Flynn's rural gloom.

h: A commuter obsessed with a couple she watches from the window sees something she shouldn't, but a drinker's memory makes a poor witness.

like.r: The template for this kind of domestic-noir bestseller, colder and more cunning.
Another heroine who cannot trust her memory, here because of amnesia that resets every day.
The classic voyeur who sees a crime from a window, wittier and far more glamorous.

h: Chief Inspector Gamache investigates a retired teacher shot by an arrow in a gentle Quebec village full of poets, bistros and old grudges.

like.r: Another warm, ensemble-driven murder mystery with a lot of heart and more jokes.
A literate, character-heavy British police novel, heavier and more brooding.
A gentle, humane approach to crime, set in Botswana rather than Quebec and more light-hearted.

h: An editor reads a late author's final Golden Age manuscript and finds the last chapter missing, and a real death shadowing the page.

like.r: The classic fair-play puzzle that Horowitz loves and then quietly twists.
A modern cosy that shares Horowitz's affectionate nod to the Golden Age.
A modern puzzle that keeps Christie's mechanics while poking fun at them.

h: A prickly ex-detective hires the author himself to write about a woman who ordered her own funeral and was strangled hours later.

like.r: The author's more elaborate book-within-a-book mystery.
The first Poirot, whose sleuth-and-chronicler setup Horowitz updates with a surly twist.
A glossy modern whodunit with a sleuth who sees what others miss.

h: Four sharp retirees in a luxury village meet weekly to study cold cases, until a real murder lands on their doorstep.

like.r: The village-mystery model with a nosy older sleuth, a little drier and more old-fashioned.
A modern cosy at heart, with the Golden Age puzzle and some bite.
A warm, gentle series centered on a clever woman and her community.

h: A symbologist and a French cryptologist race through Paris and London decoding clues about a secret the Church would kill to hide.

like.r: The earlier Langdon thriller, with a ticking clock and the Vatican as the setting.
The learned, far denser ancestor of the history-and-conspiracy puzzle.
A lighter, family-friendly hunt through American history clues.

h: Robert Langdon has a single night to find a stolen antimatter bomb hidden in Rome by a resurrected secret society.

like.r: The more famous Langdon adventure, set in Paris, with a bigger secret.
Another ticking-clock science thriller, drier and more clinical.
A glossier screen version of the same kind of chase.

h: A brilliant young lawyer lands a dream job at a Memphis firm and slowly realises the perks have a very ugly price.

like.r: Tom Cruise runs from the mob and the FBI in a taut adaptation.
A savvier, grimier defence lawyer thriller with more street-level texture.
A weightier, more morally complex legal thriller where the lawyer is the suspect.

h: A small-town Mississippi lawyer defends a Black father who killed his daughter's attackers, and the town pushes back.

like.r: The classic Southern courtroom story of race and conscience, quieter and more literary.
A star-studded adaptation with a powerful closing argument.
A more commercial, plot-driven Grisham with less moral weight.

h: Scientists race against the clock in a sealed underground lab to understand a deadly microbe that arrived on a crashed satellite.

like.r: The author's other technothriller of science run amok, with dinosaurs for a much bigger spectacle.
A cool, clinical film of the book that keeps the procedure and the dread.
A true account of an Ebola outbreak near Washington, with the same clinical dread but real.

h: A theme park of cloned dinosaurs unravels over one weekend, and a chaos theorist predicts exactly how it will happen.

like.r: A blockbuster adaptation that keeps the dread and wonder while softening the novel's cynicism.
The author's cooler, more clinical thriller about a contained outbreak.
The original dinosaur-plateau adventure, breezy and Victorian with no science-ethics warning.

h: A reclusive writer is invited to a glass house in the woods for a hen weekend, and someone has a very private grudge.

like.r: The model for every isolated-house thriller, colder and with a harder twist.
Another wedding-weekend murder with a shifting cast of narrators, more lavish and cynical.
A similar narrator who might be unreliable, with a commuter backdrop in place of a forest.

h: A glamorous wedding on a windswept Irish island, a storm, a body, and a dozen guests with something to hide.

like.r: The original isolated-island whodunit, leaner and cooler.
A smaller-scale, more claustrophobic house-party mystery, told by one voice.
A wealthy family, a corpse and an array of motives, with more laughs.

h: A famous painter shoots her husband and then never speaks again; a therapist obsessed with her silence tries to unlock her.

like.r: The same kind of twist-driven suspense about a marriage, with sharper writing.
A more sophisticated narrator drawn toward a dangerous group, and slower.
A psychiatric setting with a twist, more atmospheric and stylized.

h: A retired getaway driver turned honest mechanic is pulled back for one last heist by money troubles, and Virginia has fewer exits than it seems.

like.r: A getaway driver in a quiet, ultra-stylish crime film, more art-house and sparse.
A Black working man pulled into crime by necessity, set in an earlier decade.
A fast, violent Southern thriller, more cartoonish and less rooted in class.

h: A Houston lawyer pulls a woman from a bayou on a night of a boat cruise and finds himself in a world of oil money and union violence.

like.r: Another Black protagonist drawn into a larger conspiracy, with a more noir, period feel.
The legal-minded Southern classic, quieter but with the same belief in a conscience.
A procedural plotted with a similar mix of old wounds and institutional rot.

h: A Franciscan friar and his novice investigate a string of deaths in a remote abbey whose library hides a forbidden book.

like.r: A grimy, gripping adaptation that sheds the theological digressions.
Another intellectual crime story, modern and campus-bound but with the same erudition.
Eco's friar is a nod to Holmes, and here is the original, much briefer and brisker.

h: A scholarship student joins an elite classics circle at a Vermont college, and we learn within pages that they will kill one of their own.

like.r: Another outsider who craves a world of privilege and goes bad, leaner and more cold-blooded.
A narrator seduced by a golden circle at university, nostalgic where Tartt is poisonous.
A modern murder mystery with a similar lyrical voice and a doomed bond of friends.

h: A shy new wife arrives at Manderley, where everyone still reveres the dead first Mrs de Winter, and a housekeeper wants her gone.

like.r: A modern marriage haunted by a woman's absence, faster and far more cynical.
Hitchcock's lush, shadowy film keeps the dread and softens one big turn.
A Victorian sensation novel of secrets and impostors, longer and more melodramatic.

h: A cursed Indian diamond disappears from an English country house, and the story is pieced together from rival witnesses' accounts.

like.r: The detective story's next step, with a single genius sleuth and a more streamlined plot.
A later puzzle that borrows the many-voices country-house setup with sharper turns.
A gothic English estate with secrets from the past, more brooding.

h: A bedridden Scotland Yard inspector tackles the case of Richard III and the Princes in the Tower armed only with portraits and library books.

like.r: A longer, more difficult investigation into the past through reading and reasoning.
Another laid-up investigator who solves a case without leaving the room.
Another humane and intellectual British mystery of the same era.

h: A professional assassin plans the killing of de Gaulle while a lone policeman closes in; procedural detail drives every page.

like.r: A cool, documentary-like adaptation that matches the book's meticulous tension.
A more melancholic, character-heavy view of the same Cold War world.
A more action-heavy chase across Europe with a hero who is the quarry.

h: A Soviet submarine captain heads for American waters with a silent new sub, and an analyst has to decide whether he is defecting or attacking.

like.r: A slicker, shorter adaptation with Connery's captain and a lot less jargon.

like.t: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
like.r: The Cold War from the moral grey side, rather than the technological heroic one.
A claustrophobic submarine drama with human dread instead of geopolitics.

h: A man with no memory is pulled from the sea with a bank account number and deadly skills, and half of Europe wants him dead.

like.r: The film is leaner and more kinetic, and much of its plot is invented.
A colder, more procedural manhunt, with no amnesia.
The originals of the gentleman spy, gadget-free and more cynical, with less running.

h: A Moscow homicide detective investigates three faceless corpses in a park and slowly uncovers a conspiracy beyond the Party's tolerance.

like.t: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
like.r: A cold, bleak Cold War story from the other side's shadows.
A decent but less nuanced film adaptation if you want a Soviet procedural on screen.

like.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
like.r: Another dogged investigator pulling at a crime that implicates the powerful.

h: A Chicago prosecutor is accused of murdering a colleague he was sleeping with, and defends himself in a courtroom he knows too well.

like.r: A tense, sober adaptation with Harrison Ford and a very precise ending.
A faster, more commercial lawyer thriller with a young hero and less moral shading.
A smoother, more modern take on the lawyer as detective.

h: A psychologist, a society illustrator and a young police secretary use the earliest forensic tools to hunt a killer of boys in 1896 New York.

like.r: The modern landmark of psychological profiling, faster and more intimate.
A rough nineteenth-century New York, more violent and more operatic.
Another richly detailed historical murder mystery, more cerebral and further back in time.

h: A pediatrician whose wife was murdered eight years ago gets an email from her, and the police suspect him all over again.

like.r: Another spouse-centered mystery that tilts on a series of reveals, but meaner.
A French adaptation, quick and well-liked, with an excellent chase sequence.
A man in over his head, being hunted by those who should help him.

h: A one-legged war veteran turned private eye is hired to challenge the suicide verdict on a supermodel, in a grubby, vivid London.

like.r: The classic fair-play puzzle that this pays homage to, with a lot less swearing.
A dry, literary British private-eye story with more human comedy.

like.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
like.r: Another investigator and an unusual partner digging into a wealthy family's secrets.

t: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
h: A man wakes in a different guest's body each day at a country-house party and has eight days to solve a murder that keeps repeating.

like.r: The simpler classic of the same country-house puzzle, with nothing so strange.
The same day repeating until a man learns to use it, as a comedy instead of a thriller.
A modern take on the genre with an eye for class, easier to follow.

h: A Cambridge private investigator takes on three cold cases and finds that the murdered and the missing are woven into his own life.

like.r: A more brooding procedural that also treats the past as a living thing.
A more conventional private-eye story with a similar mix of wit and damage.
Gentler, warmer cases taken on by an equally human detective.

h: A Lagos nurse keeps cleaning up after her gorgeous younger sister, who keeps killing her boyfriends; short, deadpan and unsettling.

like.r: Another story where charm hides violence, much longer and much colder.
A darkly funny look at class and survival that swerves from comedy to horror.
Another charming murderer you can't entirely condemn, played straight.

h: Precious Ramotswe opens Botswana's first female-run detective agency and solves small human problems with tea, patience and good sense.

like.r: The classic of the village-mystery tradition, a bit more brittle and murder-heavy.
Another gentle series about a community and its secrets, with a more traditional crime.
A funny, warm murder mystery with sharp older characters.

h: A drifter and a diner owner's wife plot her husband's death and slide into each other's guilt; lean, lurid and over in an afternoon.

like.r: A sharper noir about a similarly doomed pair, drawn from Cain's other novel.
A cooler, more intricate hard-boiled classic from the same decade.
Another amoral first-person criminal who seduces the reader.

h: A drawing master meets a ghostly woman in white on a moonlit road and is drawn into a plot of stolen identity and a sinister count.

like.r: A later heir to the Victorian sensation novel, shorter and more intimate.
The author's other great novel, with a detective plot told by many voices.
Another Victorian tale of secrets and inheritance, more comic and moral.

h: Three school-gate mothers circle a scandal that ends in a death at a trivia night, with the truth hiding in the gossip.

like.r: A harder, nastier suspense about marriage.
A warmer ensemble mystery with similar jokes and a recognisable community.
Another bestselling suburban puzzle, with a more fragile narrator.

h: A whirlwind heiress descends on her stuffy London relatives and rearranges their lives, engagements and furniture; Regency farce at full speed.

like.r: A modern Regency romance with the same wit, but more openly emotional and steamy.
A meddling heroine, a bubble of high society and a rewrite of Emma, comic and breezy.
The original Regency comedy of manners that Heyer's novels are built on, drier and sharper.

h: A cynical duke buys a red-haired street boy who is secretly a girl, and a masquerade of revenge turns into love in 1750s France.

like.r: A swashbuckling disguise adventure of the same period with a dashing romantic hero.
A bigger, steamier and more violent historical love story with a time-travelling twist.
Swordplay, disguises and a love that survives everything, told with more laughter.

h: A WWII nurse touches a standing stone and wakes in 1743 Scotland, forced to marry a young Highlander and choose between two eras.

like.r: Another love defined by time travel, more melancholic and less adventurous.
A war-torn epic of a stubborn heroine, far more controversial in its politics.
The same Scottish highlands, but war-focused with a doomed hero.

h: A wallflower and a rakish duke pretend to court to escape matchmakers, and the pretense stops being pretend; Regency fun, the start of Bridgerton.

like.r: A bolder, steamier Regency with a rake who must be won over.
A Regency romance with similar humor and a castle with more comic eccentricity.
The ancestor of this kind of Regency romp, fruitier in its dialogue and chaster.

h: A shy wallflower proposes a runaway marriage of convenience to a notorious rake, and he is the one who ends up undone.

like.r: A lighter and funnier Regency, in which kisses stay near the top of the page.
A newer historical romance with a suffragist heroine and a stern duke.
The original wicked-aristocrat-reformed-by-love story, much less explicit.

h: A bookish heiress inherits a crumbling castle only to find a scarred, reclusive duke who will not leave; fairy-tale banter with a Beauty-and-the-Beast heart.

like.r: A very similar Regency mix of laughs and longing, a little more ensemble.
The tale this romance quietly plays with, sweeter and sung.
A steamier historical with a deliciously wicked hero.
